themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 41 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 9.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 349% increase (z-score: 6.12)—coinciding with a separate 833% spike in dangling street signs (7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 baseline), signaling rapid public realm degradation affecting pedestrian safety and accessibility across Crown Heights.
evidence: Street condition complaints: 41 THIS WEEK vs. 9.1 weekly average (349% increase, z-score 6.12)
Dangling street signs: 7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (833% increase, z-score 7.54)
Both categories show sustained high z-scores indicating statistical anomalies, not noise
reporting_angles: Audit which streets are most affected and whether maintenance budget cuts are responsible
Interview residents and business owners about safety hazards from deteriorating infrastructure
Cross-reference with DOB building permit data to assess whether ongoing construction is damaging streets

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Crown Heights
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints exploded to 12 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 1.9 per week—a 540% increase (z-score: 5.52)—representing the fastest-growing quality-of-life complaint in the district and potentially signaling either organized activity or declining enforcement.
evidence: Graffiti complaints: 12 THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average (540% increase, z-score 5.52)
This represents the third-largest spike in the district after street conditions and dangling signs
No corresponding Reddit discussions or local news coverage yet, suggesting emerging rather than already-reported issue
reporting_angles: Map which neighborhoods within CD 308 are being hit hardest and identify patterns (gang tags, political messages, tagging crews)
Interview NYPD and Sanitation about whether this reflects a coordinated campaign or resource shortage
Check whether graffiti complaints correlate with specific construction sites or vacant buildings

themes_detail.label: Noise Disturbances Intensifying
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from street/sidewalk activity and commercial sources surged THIS WEEK to 38 and 44 complaints respectively—223% and 126% above 8-week baselines—indicating a sharp deterioration in neighborhood livability alongside street infrastructure and graffiti spikes.
evidence: Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints: 38 THIS WEEK vs. 11.8 weekly average (223% increase, z-score 4.56)
Noise - Commercial complaints: 44 THIS WEEK vs. 19.5 weekly average (126% increase, z-score 4.61)
Combined noise complaints represent over 82 incidents this week, suggesting acute disruption event or pattern
reporting_angles: Determine if noise spike correlates with specific venues, construction sites, or entertainment venues
Interview residents about whether enforcement is responsive and whether 311 complaints are being actioned
Cross-check with for-hire vehicle complaints (also up 293% last week) to see if ride-hailing traffic is contributing

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Congestion
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 28 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 7.1 per week—a 293% spike (z-score: 4.68)—suggesting mounting frustration with rideshare congestion and potentially linking to this week's noise and street condition deterioration.
evidence: For-hire vehicle complaints: 28 LAST WEEK vs. 7.1 weekly average (293% increase, z-score 4.68)
Concurrent spike in street/sidewalk noise (223% up) and street conditions (349% up) suggest vehicle traffic may be exacerbating multiple complaints
No recent local news or Reddit discussion yet detected, suggesting underreported problem
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners about whether Uber/Lyft congestion is blocking streets and increasing noise
Request data from TLC on for-hire vehicle pickup/dropoff density in Crown Heights vs. prior year
Examine whether the FRESH Pt. 2 development at Atlantic Ave is generating additional vehicle traffic

themes_detail.label: Animal Complaints in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-park complaints spiked to 5 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.6 per week—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.11)—potentially indicating pest proliferation, inadequate park maintenance, or community awareness of an emerging issue.
evidence: Animal in a park complaints: 5 LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 5.11)
Community board has requested park building/access improvements repeatedly, suggesting parks may be understaffed or deteriorating
Limited context on what animals are involved or which parks are affected
reporting_angles: Identify which parks (Prospect Park, Lincoln Terrace) are reporting animals and determine if pest control is being deployed
Interview Parks Department about whether budget constraints are limiting animal management or park maintenance
Assess whether animal complaints are rats, pigeons, coyotes, or other species and whether they pose public health risk
